CASE 01 · MASTER'S THESIS · MEDICAL IMAGING

Self-supervised 3D bias field correction for brain MRI

Reduced preprocessing time from 4 minutes to 8 seconds per scan. Master's thesis, German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE), Bonn

before after
drag to compareT1 weighted coronal

problem

3D T1 weighted MRI contains smooth, unwanted intensity drift from scanner coil inhomogeneity. The same tissue reads brighter in one brain region than another, breaking downstream segmentation and volume measurement. Traditional methods (N4, SPM) work but are slow: 4 minutes per scan across a large cohort becomes prohibitive.

approach

A self-supervised deep learning model in PyTorch and MONAI that predicts and removes the bias field directly from the image, with no paired ground truth required. Evaluated on multiple datasets (HCP, OASIS, Miriad, Rhineland, LA5c, ADNI) using intensity homogeneity, image quality, and runtime metrics to confirm generalization.

result

Bias field error substantially lower than established correction methods. Correction time dropped from approximately 4 minutes to approximately 8 seconds per scan. Packaged and documented for integration into DZNE's MRI preprocessing workflows.

CASE 02 · CODE INTELLIGENCE

Context-driven secret detection in source code

Research Assistant, Machine Learning — TU Clausthal, Institute for Software and Systems Engineering. Deep learning reduces false positives compared to regex-only approaches.

config.py
# context aware detection API_KEY = "sk_live_9fA2c...e71"secret DB_PASS = os.getenv("DB_PASS") # regex incorrectly flags this: example_key = "sk_test_0000_docs"safe by context assert token != "PLACEHOLDER"
LSTM sequence model contextual filtering GitHub API 27,480 records

problem

Regex based secret detection flags anything matching a key pattern. Test fixtures, documentation examples, placeholders all trigger false positives. Developers learn to ignore alerts, burying real leaks in noise.

approach

DeepSecret: an LSTM model that reads code context around each candidate, not just the string itself. Trained on 27,480 records from 1,166 GitHub repositories across Java, JavaScript, Python, Ruby, and Nix. Combines sequence predictions with contextual regex filters and post processing heuristics.

result

93% average weighted precision by understanding context. Compared to TufflehUnk's 756 regex rules or voting classifier approaches, DeepSecret requires no regex maintenance while achieving higher precision and recall. Real leaks stay visible, false alarms drop.

CASE 03 · PRECISION AGRICULTURE

Extracting crop row geometry from satellite data

Research Assistant, Agricultural Robotics and Engineering — University of Bonn. Per row centrelines fitted with hybrid linear plus curve models.

Connected points by row – full field view

problem

Beyond field boundaries, the robotics team needed the exact geometry of each sugar beet row – where each row runs north to south – extracted from satellite data without a ground robot or drone pass per field.

approach

Extracted row centrelines from point cloud data and fit each row with a hybrid linear plus curve model, so straight stretches and gentle field curvature are both captured. Output is per row polylines in real UTM coordinates, colour coded by row, ready for navigation planning.

result

Clean per row geometry across the field at metre scale. Assessment of which satellite derived row detection approaches were fit for purpose, handed to the interdisciplinary team with trade offs spelled out: resolution versus row accuracy, processing cost versus coverage.

CASE 04 · REMOTE SENSING

Land cover segmentation into vegetation, water, terrain, and built up

Satellite classification with GIS tooling. Foundation for crop and field level work.

Land cover classification – full scene
vegetation water terrain, bare soil built up, other

problem

Turn raw satellite imagery of a large region into a usable map. Separate vegetation, water, terrain and built up land clearly enough to reason about what is on the ground and plan agricultural operations.

approach

Sourced Landsat 8/9 scenes over the target region through USGS EarthExplorer. Classified each pixel into land cover classes. Cross checked results against false color composites over marked regions of interest. GIS tooling tied classification back to real world coordinates.

result

Land cover segmentation separating vegetation, water, terrain and built up areas across the scene. The base layer for field and row level agricultural work to build on top of.

Computer Science master's graduate focused on deep learning across imaging, code intelligence, and satellite agriculture.

My work moves between medical imaging, code intelligence and satellite based agriculture. The throughline is the same: understand what the signal looks like before reaching for an architecture, and evaluate on more than one dataset before calling it done.

I like problems where the model must survive contact with real data: scanner quirks, satellite resolution limits, messy GitHub repos. Outside of that, I teach yoga and spend a lot of weekends hiking.
